the relative differences between the _OFR_ and the mass flow

BF difference effect could also be examined. Table 2 lists
the geometry and target TMR in the annular rings. The BF
defined in Eq. (3) describes the ratio of the sum of the pintle
orifice width to the pintle perimeter in the cross-section of the
pintle. Therefore, the BF denotes the ratio at which the propellant from the pintle orifice obstructs the annular flow. In a
two-row pintle orifice, the combustion characteristics of the
combustor can be varied depending on the distance between
the two rows [28]. Here, the distance between the two rows
was fixed as 0.5 mm to simplify the variations of the pintle
injector configuration. In the previous combustion test of a
pintle injector with BF � 86% referring to Ryu’s case [17],

Table 3 presents the geometries of the pintle orifices. For

for forced convection cooling by liquid oxygen at the hemispherical pintle tip (Fig. 3). All three pintle orifices had a
diameter of 18 mm and skip ratio ( _L_ S/ _D_ p) of 0.63, and the
mass flow ratio of the first to the second row was 82.5:17.5
based on the area ratio. For all pintle injectors, the number
of orifices in each row is 22.

**2.4** **Measurements**

It is necessary to measure the propellant mass flow rates to
evaluate the combustion performance of the pintle injector
combinations. A Coriolis flowmeter (Micro Motion™) was
used to directly acquire the liquid oxygen mass flow rate.
Turbine flowmeters (Hoffer™) were used to determine the
volume flow rate of the fuel injector (1 <sup>′′</sup> ), FCR (1/2 <sup>′′</sup> ), and
water coolant (2 <sup>′′</sup> ). The fuel flowmeters for the annular ring
and FCR were installed in duplicate to improve measurement
reliability. In addition to the volume flow, propellant densities
are necessary to calculate fuel and coolant mass flow rates.
Therefore, thermocouples and pressure transducers (Honeywell TJE series) were used before and after the flowmeters.
T-type thermocouples were applied to the oxidizer manifold and a K-type for the fuel manifold and FCR. The same
